items.title: A New Fairness Doctrine or Something Else?
items.description: A policy essay tracing debates over the public's access to information from the FCC's Fairness Doctrine to today's algorithmically curated platforms and AI systems. It weighs paths forward, from a modernized fairness obligation to public-interest duties around recommender design and amplification, and argues the country must decide how it governs access to information in an algorithmic age.

items.title: Location Technology and the U.S. Fourth Amendment
items.description: An ongoing research project examining how the Fourth Amendment, and the Supreme Court decisions that interpret it, apply to location data across technologies and types of data collection. It begins with Chatrie v. United States, which found that obtaining Google Location History through a geofence warrant crossed a constitutional line, and traces the reasoning of its majority, concurrences, and dissents. It classifies location data by source, precision, retention, and user involvement, and assesses whether data from ride-sharing apps, social media, streaming platforms, and LLM chats is covered, excluded, or still unresolved. Early findings were accepted as a poster at EAAMO 2026.
